sections.h2: Where is West Jordan, Utah, and what borders it?
sections.html:
West Jordan sits at the southwest end of the Salt Lake Valley in Salt Lake County, with the Jordan River as its eastern edge and the Oquirrh Mountains on the west. Taylorsville and Kearns lie to the north, South Jordan to the south, and Sandy, Murray and Midvale to the east.

The city covers roughly 31 to 32 square miles, depending on which figure you use, and the elevation is a little over 4,300 feet. Western neighborhoods such as Welby, Copper Hills and Jordan Hills climb the lower slopes of the Oquirrh range, so views and drainage differ a lot from the flat blocks near the river.

The 2020 census counted 116,961 people, which made West Jordan the third largest city in Utah. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate on this page is 116,812, so growth has leveled off after the jump from 68,336 in 2000 to 103,712 in 2010.

sections.h2: How did West Jordan start, and what changed in 2020?
sections.html:
Settlers arrived in the Salt Lake Valley in 1847, and the river west of Salt Lake City came to be called the Jordan. Archibald Gardner built one of the area's first sawmills in 1850, and his mill and houses were later turned into Gardner Village, a shopping district.

West Jordan was incorporated on January 10, 1941. Its population was only 2,107 in 1950 and 4,221 in 1970, then 27,192 in 1980 and 42,892 in 1990. Much of the city's housing was therefore built after 1980.

In November 2017 voters approved a council-mayor form of government, effective January 6, 2020. The mayor, Dirk Burton, serves a term running 2020 to 2028, and a seven-member council has four district seats and three at-large seats.

sections.h2: What drives the West Jordan economy?
sections.html:
West Jordan's economy began with farming, mills and mining, and it now rests on retail, health care and finance. Mountain America Credit Union, Lynco Sales and Service, SME Steel and Cyprus Credit Union are headquartered in the city.

Jordan Valley Medical Center is the main hospital and is expanding. Jordan Landing is one of the larger mixed-use developments in the Intermountain West, and the city has four major retail centers. The Kennecott copper mine, described as the largest man-made excavation in the world, is on the western edge of the city. Salt Lake Community College's Jordan Campus offers general education and health science courses.

A mix of retail, health care and finance employers means buyers can come from several fields.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit affect West Jordan houses?
sections.html:
West Jordan has freeway and rail access on its edges and a few major arterials through the middle. Interstate 15 runs just east of the city limits, and Interstate 215 runs to the northeast. Bangerter Highway crosses the middle of the city, and Redwood Road runs through the eastern part.

The Mountain View Corridor, a ten-lane route with exits at 7800 South, 9000 South and Old Bingham Highway, opened its first phase on December 15, 2012. A TRAX light rail line opened August 7, 2011, and has six stops in West Jordan on its way from Fashion Place West in Murray to Daybreak in South Jordan.

Distance to a station or an on-ramp is one of the first things buyers check. Houses beside Bangerter Highway or Redwood Road may carry traffic noise, while houses a short walk from a rail stop draw a different crowd.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve West Jordan?
sections.html:
Most of West Jordan is in the Jordan School District, and two small northern sections are in the Granite School District. Jordan School District has its headquarters at 7387 S Campus View Drive in West Jordan and enrolled about 57,866 students in 2021 and 2022.

The city has 16 elementary schools, four middle schools and two high schools, West Jordan High School and Copper Hills High School. The Jordan District lost 44 of its 84 schools in 2009 when the eastern communities formed the Canyons School District.

Ask the district to confirm the school boundary for a specific address, because a house on a district edge may feed a different school than the neighbor across the street.

sections.h2: What are West Jordan's rental and code enforcement rules?
sections.html:
Landlords in West Jordan need a General Business License and a Rental Dwelling application. The city also runs a voluntary Good Landlord Program that offers a discounted fee to owners who complete a four-hour class and keep a signed agreement, a written lease and rental applications on file. Renewal of the class is required every four years.

The city states that single-family rentals average 78% more police and fire calls a year than owner-occupied homes, and it wants at least one off-street parking space per rental unit at no extra charge. Code enforcement is at 8000 S. Redwood Road, and the main phone line is 801-569-5000. Residents can file complaints through the city's online Report a Problem form.

If you rent your West Jordan house, confirm that your license is current before you sell.

sections.h2: How do climate and fault risk affect a West Jordan house?
sections.html:
Salt Lake City, the nearest long-term weather station described in our sources, has a January average high of 38.6 degrees and a low of 24.2. July averages a high of 94.0 and a low of 68.2, and the city gets about 15.5 inches of precipitation a year and roughly 52 inches of snow.

Strong winter inversions trap air in the valley. The Utah Geological Survey notes that earthquake risk to a house depends on where the hazards are and when the house was built, which is a reason to ask about the age of the foundation and any retrofits.

  • Roof age, because snow and summer sun both wear shingles.
  • Furnace and air conditioner age.
  • Foundation cracks and drainage on hillside lots in Copper Hills and Jordan Hills.

sections.h2: How do property tax and recording work in Salt Lake County?
sections.html:
Salt Lake County property tax is due November 30, and unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1. Tax notices go out by November 1, valuation notices are mailed by July 22, and the Board of Equalization takes appeals from August 1 until September 15. All property is valued as it stood on January 1.

Utah gives a primary residence a 45% exemption on up to one acre, so the taxable value is 55% of market value. A second home or empty residential property is taxed at 100%.

Deeds are recorded at the Salt Lake County Recorder, 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, for a flat $40.00 per recording plus $2.00 for each legal description over ten. The deed should show the parcel number, the grantee's mailing address and a notary acknowledgment. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

sections.h2: What options do West Jordan sellers have?
sections.html:
West Jordan owners can list the house, sell it themselves, or ask a cash buyer for an offer, and the best route depends on the condition and the timeline. A listing suits a house in good shape that you can show for several weeks. A direct sale suits a house with deferred repairs, a tenant, a late mortgage or an estate to settle.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses in West Jordan and the rest of Utah in their present condition. We explain how an offer is built, you take your time, and you choose whether to accept it.

faqs.q: What county is West Jordan, UT in?
faqs.a: West Jordan is in Salt Lake County. Tax notices, appeals and deed recording all go through county offices in Salt Lake City.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in West Jordan?
faqs.a: Property taxes are due November 30, and unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1. Notices are mailed by November 1 each year.

faqs.q: Does West Jordan require a rental license?
faqs.a: Yes. Landlords need a General Business License and a Rental Dwelling application. The Good Landlord Program is voluntary and gives a discounted fee to owners who finish the required class.

faqs.q: Which school district is West Jordan in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in the Jordan School District. Two small northern sections are in the Granite School District.

faqs.q: Can I sell my West Jordan house without repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. No law requires you to repair a house before you sell it. A cash buyer purchases it as it stands, and you can decide after seeing an offer.
